newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bomber dies in blast at Algeria's bank plant.
newsitem.headline: Bomber dies in blast at Algeria's bank plant.

text.p: A suspected Moslem militant died when a bomb he was planting at a Central Bank banknote printing plant in Algiers blew up prematurely, Algerian newspapers said on Tuesday.
The bomber was blown up to pieces on Monday when the bomb exploded just as he began activating the device inside the plant, Le Matin daily reported.
The L'Authentique paper said one employee was wounded in the blast.
The two newspapers gave no details about how the bomber broke into the heavily guarded building.
Officials were not immediately available for comments.
The printing plant is located more than two km (one mile) away from the Central Bank headquarters in downtown Algiers.
The blast was the latest in a series of bomb attacks the Algerian authorities blame on Moslem guerrillas.
Last week Moslem rebels detonated a bomb under a passenger train, killing eight people and wounding 30 near Algiers.
At least 50,000 people have died since violence erupted in Algeria after the authorities in January 1992 scrapped a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a huge lead.
